Dear Officer:

We're wondering as to the effect of a U.S. Presidential Pardon on the admissibility of the applicant for Canadian immigration purposes. To be clear, under U.S. law, a Full and Unconditional Pardon removes all legal disabilities stemming from the conviction. As such, we're wondering if such pardons also remove any prior inadmissibility under IRPA?

There is very little guidance available on the effect of foreign pardons, and none on the effect of Presidential Pardons.

Please do not hesitate to follow-up should you require further information or clarification as to our question. Thank you greatly as always for your assistance.

Best regards,
